The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Yellow/necrotic margins forming a V-shaped pattern
- Brown necrotic tissue along leaf edges
- Green center still intact
- Some dark spots visible

This V-shaped marginal yellowing strongly suggests **Verticillium Wilt**. Let me check the part index and reference images.
Leaf part narrows to 13 classes. Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt (V-shaped marginal lesions), Early_Blight, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato. Let me view one reference per top candidate.
The LeafNet_112 Verticillium reference is very similar to the test image (broad marginal necrosis with yellow border). Let me check one more candidate class with my final view.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato leaf with broad marginal yellowing/browning, V-shaped pattern, yellow transition zone between healthy green center and brown necrotic margins, scattered dark spots.

- **Verticillium_Wilt (LeafNet_112)**: Nearly identical - broad marginal necrosis with yellow-green border, same pattern of yellow-to-brown transition. Strong match.

- **Early_Blight**: Shows distinct circular dark lesions with concentric rings - doesn't match the broad marginal pattern of the test image.

- **Bacterial_Canker (Bugwood_1)**: Shows more uniformly dried/crispy brown margins without the prominent yellow chlorotic transition zone seen in the test image.

The test image matches Verticillium Wilt's characteristic description: "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing."
